idiom_name: begin/rescue with the retry keyword, an attempts counter and a jittered sleep (or the retriable gem)
implementation_notes: Ruby is the one language that absorbs re-execution into syntax: `retry` inside a rescue clause runs the block again, so the idiom is an attempts counter plus the delay computation plus `sleep interval` (Kernel#sleep). What the keyword does not provide is the schedule, which is why this file is idiomatic rather than native here: the bare idiom is the right size for one call site, while the retriable gem computes randomized exponential intervals for you (defaults tries 3, base_interval 0.5, multiplier 1.5, rand_factor 0.5, max_interval 60, max_elapsed_time 900 seconds) and yields the try number to the block. Note that retriable 5.x publishes its configuration as a frozen snapshot, so changes go through Retriable.configure.
code_sketch:
attempts = 0
begin
  client.call
rescue IOError, Timeout::Error => e
  attempts += 1
  raise if attempts >= 5
  ceiling = [0.5 * (2**(attempts - 1)), 30].min
  sleep(rand * ceiling)          # full jitter
  retry
end
pitfalls: retry without an attempts counter restarts the block forever, and it re-executes the whole begin block, so any work before the failing call is repeated as well.
retriable 5.x freezes the published configuration: mutate it through Retriable.configure, never by assigning to Retriable.config fields.
sleep blocks the thread (including the GVL-holding thread) for the whole delay, so a long backoff in a threaded server (Puma) occupies a worker instead of yielding it.
